name: Mordecai
overview: Mordecai is a male figure noted for returning to Judah after the Babylonian captivity, as recorded in Ezra 2:2 and Nehemiah 7:7. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional personal notes provided about him. His return signifies his participation in the restoration of the Jewish community in Jerusalem following exile.
namesAndTitles: The name Mordecai is a proper name meaning 'Marduk,' which is referenced in Ezra 2:2. This name reflects a connection to a Babylonian deity, indicating the cultural context in which he lived, though it was not given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Mordecai as a descendant of Jacob, as inferred from Ezra 2:2. Beyond this lineage, there are no other recorded family relationships for Mordecai in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mordecai's significance lies in his role as one who returned with the Jewish exiles to Judah, contributing to the reestablishment of God's people in their land after captivity. His mention in the genealogical records underscores the continuity of the covenant community through the trials of exile and restoration.
